catalogue: Australian residential external windows and glazed doors

objects.name: external window assembly
objects.definition: A complete factory-made or site-documented window product fitted into an external wall opening, including its perimeter frame, fixed or moving glazed parts, seals, drainage paths, hardware and installation fixings.
functions: Transmit daylight while closed
Provide controlled ventilation where openable
Resist assigned wind, air and water actions as a complete product

ncc_references.relationship: Covered external window assemblies are designed, constructed and installed through the AS 2047 and Housing Provisions Part 8.2 pathway within its stated limits.

cad.pattern: One scheduled product per wall opening, with repeated lights or sashes inside the perimeter frame
cad.placement: Within a prepared external wall opening
cad.opening: Occupies and seals a rough wall opening without carrying wall gravity loads
cad.load: Transfers its assigned wind actions to framing beside the opening

notes: Window compliance belongs to the tested and installed assembly, not to a visually similar collection of profiles.

objects.name: fixed window assembly
objects.definition: A window assembly whose glass or glazed light is permanently retained in the frame and has no sash intended to open for ventilation.
functions: Transmit daylight
Provide a weather-resistant transparent or translucent wall opening
Avoid moving joints and operating hardware

ncc_references.relationship: Fixed external windows are within the covered window-assembly family unless a stated exclusion applies.

cad.pattern: One or more non-opening glazed lights within a perimeter frame
cad.placement: Within an external wall opening
cad.opening: Fills the wall opening without an operable ventilation gap
cad.load: Window assembly transferring face actions to the opening sides

notes: A fixed light may be glazed directly into the main frame or held in a non-operating sash; the product detail decides which components exist.

objects.name: operable window assembly
objects.definition: A window assembly with at least one sash, blade or other part designed to move so the closed window can be opened for ventilation or access.
functions: Transmit daylight
Provide controllable natural ventilation
Close and seal the opening against normal external conditions

ncc_references.relationship: Some openable windows require fall protection and edge sealing according to location and project conditions.

cad.pattern: At least one moving sash or blade inside a fixed perimeter frame
cad.placement: Within an external wall opening
cad.opening: Creates a controllable ventilation opening
cad.load: Moving part transfers actions through hardware and frame when closed

notes: Store opening geometry separately from the nominal window size.

objects.name: awning window assembly
objects.definition: An operable window whose sash is hinged or pivoted about a horizontal axis at or near its top and projects outward at the bottom.
functions: Provide outward-opening ventilation
Use a compression closing edge around much of the sash
Shed some direct rain while partly open

cad.pattern: One or more outward-projecting top-hung sashes
cad.placement: Within a window frame
cad.opening: Swept volume projects outside the wall
cad.load: Sash supported by hinges or stays and locked into the frame

objects.name: casement window assembly
objects.definition: An operable window whose sash opens inward or outward about a vertical hinge or pivot axis at one side.
functions: Provide side-hung ventilation
Create a large clear opening when fully open
Close the sash against perimeter seals

cad.pattern: One or more side-hung glazed sashes
cad.placement: Within a window frame
cad.opening: Swept volume lies inside or outside according to handing
cad.load: Sash supported along one side by hardware

objects.name: hopper window assembly
objects.definition: An operable window whose sash is hinged at the bottom and opens from the top, most commonly inward but sometimes outward in a documented product.
functions: Provide top-edge ventilation
Retain the sash at a controlled opening angle
Close against frame seals

cad.pattern: One or more bottom-hung sashes opening at the head
cad.placement: Within a window frame
cad.opening: Swept volume usually projects into the room
cad.load: Sash retained by bottom hinges and side stays

objects.name: horizontal sliding window assembly
objects.definition: An operable window with one or more sashes that move horizontally along tracks within the plane of the frame, usually past a fixed or another sliding sash.
functions: Provide ventilation without an outward swing
Guide moving sashes on tracks
Close interlocking or meeting stiles against weatherseals

cad.pattern: Overlapping fixed and sliding sashes on horizontal tracks
cad.placement: Within a window frame
cad.opening: Clear opening grows within the frame plane
cad.load: Sashes supported at tracks and restrained by interlocks and locks

objects.name: single-hung window assembly
objects.definition: A vertically sliding window with a movable lower sash and a stationary upper sash or fixed light.
functions: Provide vertical sliding ventilation
Counterbalance the moving lower sash
Close at the sill and meeting rail

cad.pattern: Lower moving sash passing the stationary upper light
cad.placement: Within vertical sash channels
cad.end: Lower sash raised to opening limit
cad.opening: Ventilation opening forms below the raised sash
cad.load: Moving sash counterbalanced and guided at both jambs

objects.name: double-hung window assembly
objects.definition: A vertically sliding window with two glazed sashes, where the lower sash rises and the upper sash lowers in separate tracks.
functions: Provide controllable top or bottom ventilation
Counterbalance both moving sashes
Seal the two sashes together at meeting rails

cad.pattern: Two vertically sliding sashes passing in separate channels
cad.placement: Within a deep window frame or box frame
cad.end: Independent upper and lower opening limits
cad.opening: Ventilation may form above, below or at both ends
cad.load: Each sash is guided and counterbalanced at the jambs

objects.name: pivot window assembly
objects.definition: An operable window whose sash rotates about pivot hardware near the middle of its jambs or its head and sill instead of using hinges at an edge.
functions: Provide ventilation by rotating the sash
Allow reversible access to glass faces in some products
Support the sash at opposed pivot points

cad.pattern: One rotating sash on two opposed pivot fittings
cad.placement: Within a window frame
cad.opening: Swept volume may project to both sides of the wall
cad.load: Sash weight and actions concentrated at pivot hardware

objects.name: adjustable louvre window assembly
objects.definition: A window assembly containing a series of overlapping horizontal or vertical blades that rotate together between open and closed positions to control ventilation.
functions: Provide adjustable ventilation
Overlap blades to close the opening
Coordinate blades, clips, operating bar, frame and seals as one product

ncc_references.relationship: Adjustable louvres are included in the AS 2047 covered assembly family; fixed louvres are treated separately.

cad.pattern: Repeated overlapping blades linked to one operator
cad.placement: Within a louvre frame in a wall opening
cad.opening: Blade rotation creates repeated ventilation slots
cad.load: Blades supported by clips or end mechanisms within the frame

notes: A blade may be glass or another material; the complete external louvre product still needs its applicable evidence path.

objects.name: one-piece-framed window wall assembly
objects.definition: A large multi-light glazed wall product, often floor-to-ceiling and horizontally continuous, whose perimeter and intermediate framing are made as one coordinated window system.
functions: Form a predominantly glazed part of an external wall
Divide large glazing into supported lights
Transfer glazing and frame actions through one tested system

ncc_references.relationship: Window walls with one-piece framing are included in the stated AS 2047 pathway.

cad.pattern: Storey-height or large multi-light grid
cad.placement: Within or across a large external wall opening
cad.start: Lower perimeter frame or slab interface
cad.end: Upper perimeter frame or head interface
cad.opening: Replaces a broad portion of opaque wall
cad.load: Non-loadbearing glazed wall system transferring face actions to building structure

notes: Do not equate this NCC one-piece-framing category with every curtain-wall or site-built facade system.

objects.name: box or faceted bay window assembly
objects.definition: A projecting window arrangement made from a front window and return or angled side windows, forming a rectangular, segmented or faceted bay outside the main wall plane.
functions: Project glazing beyond the wall face
Increase outlook and internal ledge or floor area
Coordinate several window units with structural and weathering junctions

cad.pattern: Three or more coupled window faces projecting from the main wall plane
cad.placement: At a formed external wall projection
cad.opening: Occupies a multi-plane rough opening or framed projection
cad.load: Window products supported by separately designed head, base and corner framing

notes: The projecting building structure, roof and base are not supplied automatically by the window object.

objects.name: external framed glazed door assembly
objects.definition: A complete external door product with a perimeter frame and one or more moving or fixed panels containing glass, including threshold, hardware, seals, drainage and installation fixings.
functions: Provide a closable passage through an external wall
Transmit daylight through glazed panels
Resist assigned wind, air and water actions as a complete framed product

ncc_references.relationship: Framed sliding and swinging glazed doors, including framed French and bi-fold doors, are within the stated AS 2047 pathway.

cad.pattern: One or more moving leaves or panels and optional fixed panels in a perimeter frame
cad.placement: Within an external wall doorway opening
cad.opening: Creates a trafficable doorway when the moving panel opens
cad.load: Door product transfers face actions and operating loads through frame fixings

notes: This family is deliberately limited to framed glazed external doors; opaque doors and frameless glass doors need separate paths.

objects.name: hinged external glazed door assembly
objects.definition: A framed external glazed door with one moving leaf that swings about hinges fixed along one vertical edge.
functions: Provide a side-hung external passage
Close against jamb and threshold seals
Carry leaf weight and operating forces through hinges

cad.pattern: Single swinging glazed leaf in a perimeter frame
cad.placement: Within an external doorway
cad.opening: Door swing creates a swept traffic zone
cad.load: Leaf supported by hinges and frame jamb

objects.name: external glazed French door set
objects.definition: A framed pair of hinged glazed door leaves that meet at their central stiles without a fixed mullion, or a single narrow hinged glazed door made in the same form.
functions: Provide a wide hinged opening
Close paired leaves at meeting stiles
Transfer leaf loads through perimeter-frame fixings without a centre mullion
not_synonyms: door pair with centre mullion automatically

cad.pattern: One or two side-hung glazed leaves, commonly a centre-opening pair
cad.placement: Within an external door frame
cad.opening: One or both leaves sweep outward or inward
cad.load: Leaves rely on hinges and perimeter-frame attachment; no centre mullion is assumed

notes: The absence of a fixed centre mullion is a modelling distinction, not only a style label.

objects.name: external bi-fold glazed door assembly
objects.definition: A framed external glazed door in which two or more leaves are hinged together and guided so they fold and stack toward one or both sides of the opening.
functions: Create a wide opening with folded leaves
Guide connected panels along a track
Close multiple panel joints with locks and seals

cad.pattern: Hinged chain of glazed leaves guided to fold and stack
cad.placement: Within a wide external door frame
cad.opening: Panels sweep and fold across a combined stacking zone
cad.load: Leaf weight carried by documented pivots, carriers and tracks

notes: Carrier and pivot geometry is product-specific and must not be invented from panel count alone.

objects.name: external sliding glazed door assembly
objects.definition: A framed external glazed door with one or more moving panels that travel horizontally on tracks past fixed or other moving panels.
functions: Provide a large opening without a door swing
Support moving panels on rollers and tracks
Close interlocking stiles, jambs and threshold against weatherseals

cad.pattern: Overlapping fixed and moving glazed panels on parallel tracks
cad.placement: Within a wide external door opening
cad.end: Maximum panel slide or stack position
cad.opening: Traffic opening forms within the frame plane
cad.load: Moving panels supported on rollers or carriers and restrained at head and interlocks

objects.name: window perimeter frame
objects.definition: The fixed supporting surround of a window, normally made from a head, two jambs and a sill, into which fixed glazing, sashes and hardware are fitted.
functions: Define the window perimeter
Support fixed and moving window parts
Transfer window actions to the building opening

cad.pattern: Closed perimeter with optional intermediate members
cad.placement: At the boundary of the window product
cad.opening: Surrounds all glazed and operable lights
cad.load: Structural window component carrying actions to frame fixings

objects.name: external glazed door frame
objects.definition: The fixed supporting surround of a framed glazed door, normally including a head, two jambs and a sill or threshold, with tracks, stops or rebates suited to its moving panels.
functions: Define and support the doorway product
Receive hinges, tracks, locks and seals
Transfer door actions to the building opening

cad.pattern: Closed or threshold-open perimeter suited to the door operation
cad.placement: At the boundary of the glazed door product
cad.opening: Surrounds the traffic opening and panels
cad.load: Structural product component carrying actions and hardware loads to fixings

objects.name: window or door frame head
objects.definition: The fixed horizontal member across the top of a window or glazed-door perimeter frame.
functions: Close the top of the product frame
Receive glazing, sash, panel, track or seal details
Transfer top-frame actions toward the jambs and fixings

cad.pattern: Single horizontal perimeter member
cad.placement: Across the top of the product frame below the rough-opening head
cad.opening: Forms the upper boundary of the product opening
cad.load: Window or door frame member, not the wall lintel

notes: The frame head must remain distinct from the structural lintel above it and the flashing outside it.

objects.name: window or door frame jamb
objects.definition: Either fixed vertical side member of a window or glazed-door perimeter frame.
functions: Form a side of the product frame
Receive sash, panel, hardware, seals and installation fixings
Transfer product actions to framing beside the opening

cad.pattern: Paired vertical perimeter members
cad.placement: At the sides of the product frame
cad.opening: Forms a side boundary of the product opening
cad.load: Primary path for product actions to adjacent wall framing

objects.name: window frame sill
objects.definition: The fixed horizontal bottom member of a window perimeter frame, commonly shaped to support glazing or sashes and manage water toward the exterior.
functions: Close and support the bottom of the window frame
Receive lower glazing or sash details
Collect and discharge water through the product drainage path

cad.pattern: Single horizontal lower frame member
cad.placement: At the bottom of the window product
cad.opening: Forms the lower boundary and drainage edge of the product
cad.load: Supports product parts and passes actions to jambs and sill support

notes: The window sill is part of the product; sill flashing sits outside or beneath it as a separate weathering object.

objects.name: external glazed door threshold
objects.definition: The horizontal bottom member or trafficable sill of a glazed-door frame, shaped to guide, seal or support the door panel while allowing people to cross the opening.
functions: Form the lower door-frame boundary
Receive tracks, seals or panel closure
Manage water and traffic across the doorway

cad.pattern: Single continuous lower frame member across the doorway
cad.placement: At finished-floor or documented step-down level
cad.opening: Crossed by occupants when the door is open
cad.load: Supports door tracks or closure and requires continuous building support

notes: Threshold height, step-down and accessible-path rules are project constraints, not one universal profile.

objects.name: window or door frame mullion
objects.definition: A fixed vertical intermediate framing member that divides adjacent window or glazed-door units or lights and transfers their actions toward the perimeter frame.
functions: Divide the glazed opening vertically
Support adjacent glazing, sashes or panels
Transfer face actions to the perimeter frame

cad.pattern: Vertical intermediate member repeated at the product module grid
cad.placement: Between adjacent lights or units
cad.opening: Separates side-by-side glazed fields
cad.load: Structural product member transferring face actions to the perimeter

objects.name: window coupling mullion
objects.definition: A vertical coupling member designed to join two separate window units while providing the required alignment and structural connection between them.
functions: Join adjacent window units
Maintain a controlled joint and alignment
Transfer combined unit actions through the documented coupler

cad.pattern: Continuous vertical joint member between factory window frames
cad.placement: At abutting jambs of adjacent window units
cad.opening: Joins rather than divides a single factory frame
cad.load: Documented structural or non-structural window coupler

notes: A cosmetic cover over abutting frames is not automatically a load-carrying coupling mullion.

objects.name: window or door frame transom
objects.definition: A fixed horizontal intermediate framing member that divides a window or glazed-door assembly into lights or panels above and below.
functions: Divide the glazed opening horizontally
Support adjacent glazing, sashes or panels
Transfer actions toward jambs or mullions

cad.pattern: Horizontal intermediate member at scheduled light divisions
cad.placement: Between jambs or mullions
cad.opening: Separates upper and lower glazed fields
cad.load: Structural product member transferring face actions to vertical frame members

objects.name: window coupling pipe staunchion
objects.definition: A load-bearing pipe or hollow support inserted at a joint between separate windows to strengthen a straight or angled coupled-window arrangement.
functions: Strengthen a coupled window joint
Carry face actions between units and supports
Provide a core for coupling cover plates

cad.pattern: Vertical concealed or partly concealed support at a coupled unit joint
cad.placement: Between adjacent window jambs
cad.opening: Occupies the coupling joint, not the clear light
cad.load: Load-bearing coupling support

objects.name: window coupling cover plate
objects.definition: A usually vertical trim plate fitted over the joint between two window units to cover the junction, with or without a separate structural pipe staunchion behind it.
functions: Cover the visible coupled-window joint
Protect or finish joint seals and fixings
Accommodate straight or angled unit connections

cad.pattern: Continuous cover over a vertical window-unit joint
cad.placement: On one or both faces of coupled frames
cad.opening: Covers the coupling joint
cad.load: Normally a finish or weathering cover unless documented otherwise

objects.name: factory-fitted timber window reveal
objects.definition: A timber surround fitted to the inside of an aluminium or other window or door product to extend it through the wall thickness and provide a fixing and lining interface.
functions: Extend the product frame to the internal wall face
Provide a substrate for fixing and architraves
Form the finished sides, head and sill of the opening reveal

cad.pattern: Four-sided or three-sided timber surround behind the product frame
cad.placement: From the inner face of the window or door frame toward the internal lining
cad.opening: Lines the depth of the wall opening
cad.load: Installation and lining support, not a substitute for the wall lintel or jamb studs

notes: In Australian window practice, lining board may be loose language for this item, but the actual product and location should be confirmed.

objects.name: window frame cavity closure section
objects.definition: An applied section fitted at a frame jamb or perimeter to extend the window or door frame across or into a wall cavity and close the otherwise open return.
functions: Extend frame depth across a cavity
Close and finish the cavity return
Provide a controlled interface for lining, masonry or seals

cad.pattern: Applied perimeter section where frame depth does not span the wall return
cad.placement: At the inside or side of a product frame beside a wall cavity
cad.opening: Closes the cavity edge around the opening
cad.load: Non-primary closure unless documented as structural

objects.name: integral window nailing fin
objects.definition: A thin integral flange projecting from a window or patio-door frame and lapping the wall framing or sheathing so fasteners can secure the product around its perimeter.
functions: Locate the product against the wall face
Provide a perimeter fastening flange
Coordinate the frame with weather barrier and flashing layers

cad.pattern: Perimeter flange around selected sides of the product frame
cad.placement: Between product frame and wall weathering layers
cad.opening: Laps the face around the rough opening
cad.load: Product fixing flange carrying scheduled actions through fasteners

notes: An integral fin may contribute to fixing or flashing, but the complete opening-flashing detail still decides its weathering role.

objects.name: window or door frame fixing lug
objects.definition: A discrete bracket attached to a window or door frame and fastened back to the building structure to hold the product in its opening.
functions: Connect the product frame to the building
Transfer local frame actions to structural supports
Allow concealed fixing where a perimeter fin is not used

cad.pattern: Discrete brackets at scheduled frame positions
cad.placement: Between product frame and rough-opening structure
cad.opening: Spans the installation gap locally
cad.load: Transfers product actions to the building frame or masonry

objects.name: external window storm mould
objects.definition: An applied external perimeter section that covers and seals the joint between a window frame and the surrounding building, often incorporating a small flashing fin.
functions: Cover the external frame-to-wall joint
Deflect surface water away from the joint
Provide a finished perimeter trim and seal interface

cad.pattern: External trim run around selected product-frame edges
cad.placement: Over the frame-to-wall perimeter joint
cad.opening: Follows the external opening perimeter
cad.load: Weathering and finishing section unless separately documented

objects.name: window sill flap seal
objects.definition: A flexible flap fitted beneath a window sill to close a variable gap between the product and supporting construction as the building or frame moves within its design allowance.
functions: Take up limited variation beneath the sill
Reduce direct air or water entry at the lower joint
Maintain a flexible contact with adjacent construction

cad.pattern: Continuous flexible strip beneath the window sill
cad.placement: Between sill underside and adjacent construction
cad.opening: Closes part of the lower installation joint without blocking drainage
cad.load: Flexible seal, not structural sill support

objects.name: window or door frame packer
objects.definition: A small durable shim placed between a window or door product and its rough opening to hold the frame straight, level and at the required installation gap while it is fixed.
functions: Support and align the product frame
Maintain the installation gap
Prevent frame distortion at fixing points

ncc_references.relationship: Window packing is located along the sides and bottom, fixed to keep the frame straight and kept clear of flashing material.

cad.pattern: Discrete shims at scheduled side and sill positions
cad.placement: In the installation gap between product and rough opening
cad.opening: Locally occupies the perimeter installation gap
cad.load: Local alignment and support piece; capacity depends on material and detail

notes: This is not the same as a setting block supporting a glass pane inside a glazing pocket.

objects.name: window or door frame fixing
objects.definition: A screw, nail, masonry anchor or other scheduled fastener that secures a window or door frame, reveal, fin or lug to the building structure.
functions: Hold the product in its prepared opening
Transfer window or door actions to the building
Maintain frame alignment at documented fixing points

cad.pattern: Discrete repeated fixings around jambs, head and sill as scheduled
cad.placement: Through frame, reveal, fin or lug into structural support
cad.opening: Crosses the perimeter installation joint
cad.load: Mechanical connection transferring product actions

notes: Fastener size and spacing come from the tested product, wind actions, substrate and fixing guide, not from this ontology record.

objects.name: window head settlement gap
objects.definition: The deliberate clear space between the top of a window assembly and loadbearing wall framing or masonry above, retained so building loads and settlement are not transferred into the window.
functions: Separate the window from building gravity loads
Allow limited settlement or deflection above the opening
Provide space for compatible non-loadbearing seals or flashings

ncc_references.relationship: A clear head gap separates the window assembly from loadbearing framing or masonry and may need to increase for settlement over wide openings.

cad.pattern: Continuous clear horizontal slot above the product head
cad.placement: Between window head and rough-opening head or lintel zone
cad.opening: Is the controlled installation void itself
cad.load: Must remain non-loadbearing

notes: Numeric clearance is a project rule and must be taken from the applicable NCC path and installation detail.

objects.name: window frame drainage opening
objects.definition: A formed hole or slot in a window sill or frame chamber that lets collected water move toward and discharge at the exterior face.
functions: Drain water from frame chambers or tracks
Relieve collected water to the outside
Keep the internal frame face from becoming the intended discharge point

cad.pattern: Repeated holes or slots at low points in the frame drainage path
cad.placement: Through the exterior wall of sill or track chambers
cad.opening: Is a required void through the frame profile
cad.load: No load role; must remain unobstructed

notes: Do not fill modeled drainage openings with perimeter sealant, packers or finishes.

objects.name: window or door frame thermal break
objects.definition: A low-conductance element placed between more conductive inner and outer parts of a frame profile to reduce direct heat flow through the frame.
functions: Interrupt the conductive path through a metal frame
Join inner and outer profile portions
Improve the thermal behaviour of the complete window or door product

cad.pattern: Continuous strip or web within thermally broken frame profiles
cad.placement: Between interior and exterior conductive frame portions
cad.opening: Follows the frame perimeter and intermediate members
cad.load: Part of the engineered composite frame section

notes: A powder coating or ordinary gasket does not make a metal frame thermally broken.

objects.name: window sash
objects.definition: The inner frame that holds glass in an operable or sometimes fixed part of a window, normally made from rails and stiles joined around the glazing.
functions: Retain the glass as one window subassembly
Connect glazing to operating hardware or the main frame
Carry local glazing and operating actions

cad.pattern: Rectangular or shaped inner frame around a glazed light
cad.placement: Inside the main window frame
cad.opening: Moves or remains fixed according to the product
cad.load: Carries glass actions to hardware or main frame

notes: Australian door terminology commonly uses panel or leaf rather than sash for the moving glazed door part.

objects.name: awning sash
objects.definition: A glazed sash that pivots about a horizontal axis at or near its top so its bottom edge projects outward.
functions: Form the moving part of an awning window
Carry glazing between top-hung hardware and locks
Close against perimeter weatherseals

cad.pattern: One rectangular sash per awning light
cad.placement: Within an awning window frame
cad.opening: Projects outward through an arc
cad.load: Supported by stays or hinges at upper sides

objects.name: casement sash
objects.definition: A glazed sash that opens inward or outward about a vertical hinge or pivot axis along one side.
functions: Form the moving part of a casement window
Carry glazing from hinge side to lock side
Close against perimeter weatherseals

cad.pattern: One rectangular sash per casement light
cad.placement: Within a casement window frame
cad.opening: Swings through a side-hung arc
cad.load: Supported along one vertical side

objects.name: hopper sash
objects.definition: A glazed sash hinged along its bottom edge so the top opens inward or outward and is retained by side hardware.
functions: Form the moving part of a hopper window
Carry glazing above the bottom hinge
Limit and secure the top-edge opening

cad.pattern: One rectangular sash per hopper light
cad.placement: Within a hopper window frame
cad.opening: Top edge moves through an arc
cad.load: Supported at the bottom and retained at the sides

objects.name: horizontal sliding window sash
objects.definition: A glazed window sash that travels sideways within a horizontal track to open or close part of the window.
functions: Carry glazing while sliding
Engage the sill and head tracks
Close against a jamb, meeting stile or interlock

cad.pattern: One or more moving sashes overlapping fixed or moving lights
cad.placement: In horizontal tracks within the main frame
cad.opening: Moves within the frame plane
cad.load: Supported by sill track and restrained at head

objects.name: vertically sliding hung sash
objects.definition: A glazed sash that moves vertically in jamb channels and is counterbalanced by a spring balance, cord and weight or another documented mechanism.
functions: Carry glazing while moving vertically
Engage jamb guides and meeting rails
Remain controllable through counterbalance hardware

cad.pattern: One or two vertical moving sashes in separate jamb channels
cad.placement: Within a hung-window frame
cad.start: Closed sill, head or meeting-rail position
cad.opening: Slides parallel to the wall plane
cad.load: Counterbalanced and guided along both jambs

objects.name: pivot window sash
objects.definition: A glazed sash supported by opposed pivot fittings located near the middle of its stiles or rails so the sash can rotate within the main frame.
functions: Carry glass while rotating about a central axis
Connect to opposed pivot hardware
Close against a shaped perimeter seal

cad.pattern: One rotating glazed sash
cad.placement: Within a pivot window frame
cad.opening: Sweeps to both sides according to pivot location
cad.load: Concentrated at pivot fittings

objects.name: window sash top rail
objects.definition: The horizontal member across the top of a window sash.
functions: Close the top of the sash frame
Retain the upper glass edge
Connect the sash stiles and receive relevant hardware or seals

cad.pattern: One upper horizontal member per sash
cad.placement: At the top edge of a window sash
cad.opening: Bounds the top of the sash light
cad.load: Sash member carrying glazing and operating actions

objects.name: window sash bottom rail
objects.definition: The horizontal member across the bottom of a window sash.
functions: Close the bottom of the sash frame
Support or retain the lower glass edge
Connect the sash stiles and receive locks, rollers or seals where detailed

cad.pattern: One lower horizontal member per sash
cad.placement: At the bottom edge of a window sash
cad.opening: Bounds the bottom of the sash light
cad.load: Sash member supporting glazing and operating actions

objects.name: window sash stile
objects.definition: Either vertical side member of a window sash, joining its top and bottom rails around the glass.
functions: Form a vertical side of the sash
Retain a glass edge
Receive hinges, pivots, locks, interlocks or guides as detailed

cad.pattern: Paired vertical members per sash
cad.placement: At the sides of a window sash
cad.opening: Bounds a side of the sash light
cad.load: Sash member transferring glazing and hardware actions

objects.name: hung-window meeting rail
objects.definition: Either of the horizontal sash members that overlap or meet when the upper and lower sashes of a hung window are closed.
functions: Close the joint between hung sashes
Provide an interlocking or sealed overlap
Receive the sash lock where detailed

cad.pattern: Paired horizontal members aligned at the closed sash junction
cad.placement: At the top of the lower sash and bottom of the upper sash
cad.opening: Separates upper and lower sash lights
cad.load: May act structurally in the tested window system

objects.name: sliding glazed door opening panel
objects.definition: The framed glazed panel of a sliding door that moves along a track to create or close the traffic opening.
functions: Carry door glass while sliding
Create the traffic opening
Engage jamb, interlock, track, rollers, lock and seals

cad.pattern: One or more moving panels on a track
cad.placement: Within a sliding glazed-door frame
cad.opening: Moves within the door-frame plane
cad.load: Panel weight supported by rollers or carriers

objects.name: sliding glazed door fixed panel
objects.definition: A framed glazed panel in a sliding-door assembly that remains stationary while an adjacent opening panel slides past or stacks beside it.
functions: Form a fixed glazed part of the door assembly
Receive or align with an interlocking stile
Transfer glazing actions to the door frame

cad.pattern: Stationary panel beside one or more sliding panels
cad.placement: Within a sliding glazed-door frame
cad.opening: Does not move to create the traffic opening
cad.load: Glazed panel supported directly by the door frame

objects.name: glazed door panel top rail
objects.definition: The horizontal member across the top of a framed glazed door panel or leaf.
functions: Close the top of the panel frame
Retain the upper glass edge
Connect the panel stiles and receive guides or seals where detailed

cad.pattern: One upper horizontal member per framed door panel
cad.placement: At the top of the door panel
cad.opening: Bounds the top of the panel glass
cad.load: Door-panel member carrying glazing and operating actions

objects.name: glazed door panel bottom rail
objects.definition: The horizontal member across the bottom of a framed glazed door panel or leaf, often deeper where it contains rollers or provides a robust lower edge.
functions: Close the bottom of the panel frame
Support or retain the lower glass edge
Receive rollers, pivots, seals or guides where detailed

cad.pattern: One lower horizontal member per framed door panel
cad.placement: At the bottom of the door panel
cad.opening: Bounds the bottom of the panel glass
cad.load: Door-panel member supporting glazing and operating hardware

objects.name: sliding glazed door lock stile
objects.definition: The vertical edge member of a moving sliding-door panel that closes against the frame jamb and contains or engages the door lock.
functions: Form the closing edge of the moving panel
Receive lock and handle hardware
Seal against the lock jamb

cad.pattern: One closing-edge stile per moving sliding-door panel
cad.placement: At the panel edge that meets the frame jamb
cad.opening: Defines one side of the panel glass
cad.load: Panel member carrying lock and closing forces

objects.name: sliding glazed door interlock stile
objects.definition: One of the matching vertical members on adjacent fixed and moving sliding-door panels that engage when the door is closed.
functions: Engage adjacent panels at the closed overlap
Restrain relative face movement
Carry seals and transfer local wind actions between panels

cad.pattern: Paired opposed vertical profiles at overlapping panels
cad.placement: At the closed overlap between sliding-door panels
cad.opening: Defines the internal edges of adjoining panel glass
cad.load: Can act as a structural meeting member in the tested door system

objects.name: French-door meeting stile
objects.definition: Either of the central vertical edge members where paired French-door leaves meet and close without a fixed mullion between them.
functions: Close the joint between paired leaves
Receive seals, latch, lock or bolts
Transfer closing and wind actions between active and inactive leaves

cad.pattern: Paired vertical closing edges at the centre of a French-door set
cad.placement: Where active and inactive leaves meet
cad.opening: Disappears from the clear opening when both leaves are open
cad.load: Door-leaf member receiving closing and locking forces

objects.name: window operating hardware set
objects.definition: The coordinated fittings used to connect, open, hold, close, lock and stop an operable window sash, selected for the product type and sash size.
functions: Support and guide sash movement
Control opening and closing
Secure the sash in closed or limited-open positions

cad.pattern: Matched discrete fittings at product-specific locations
cad.placement: Between operable sash and main frame
cad.opening: Controls the sash movement path
cad.load: Carries sash weight, wind and operating actions as documented

notes: Hardware capacity and locations are tied to the tested window system.

objects.name: window hinge or friction stay
objects.definition: A pivoting multi-link or hinge fitting joining an awning or casement sash to its frame and controlling the path and resistance of opening.
functions: Support the moving sash
Define its hinge axis and opening path
Hold or resist the sash at intermediate positions

cad.pattern: Paired fittings at sash sides or top and bottom
cad.placement: Between awning or casement sash and frame
cad.opening: Articulates through the sash swing
cad.load: Supports sash weight and operating actions

objects.name: window chain winder or operator
objects.definition: A manually or mechanically operated device fixed to the window frame that pushes or pulls an awning or casement sash through a chain, arm or geared linkage.
functions: Open and close the sash
Hold the sash at selected positions
Transfer user force through a controlled mechanism

cad.pattern: One or more operators per sash according to width and product
cad.placement: On frame sill, jamb or head connected to the moving sash
cad.opening: Extends and retracts with sash movement
cad.load: Operating device, not the primary sash hinge

objects.name: hung-window sash balance
objects.definition: A usually spring-loaded mechanical device in a single- or double-hung window that counterbalances the weight of a moving sash.
functions: Offset sash weight
Make vertical opening and closing controllable
Hold the sash at selected positions

cad.pattern: One balance at each side of a moving hung sash
cad.placement: Concealed or exposed in the frame jamb channel
cad.opening: Extends or changes force through vertical sash travel
cad.load: Counterbalances sash mass

objects.name: hung-window sash cord
objects.definition: A rope, cord or chain connecting a traditional hung-window sash to a concealed counterweight over a pulley.
functions: Suspend the sash weight connection
Transmit counterweight force to the sash
Travel over the sash pulley during opening

cad.pattern: One cord at each side of each traditionally weighted sash
cad.placement: From sash over pulley into weight pocket
cad.opening: Moves within pulley and weight-pocket clearances
cad.load: Tension connector carrying counterweight force

objects.name: hung-window sash weight
objects.definition: A concealed mass in a traditional double-hung or single-hung window, connected to a sash by cord or chain to counterbalance its weight.
functions: Counterbalance the moving sash
Travel vertically in a frame weight pocket
Reduce the force needed to hold and move the sash

cad.pattern: One concealed counterweight per sash side
cad.placement: In a vertical pocket beside the hung sash
cad.opening: Requires a clear weight pocket
cad.load: Gravity counterbalance mass

notes: Existing lead weights require appropriate hazardous-material handling; the ontology does not prescribe reuse.

objects.name: sliding window or door panel roller
objects.definition: A wheel or roller carriage fitted to a sliding sash or door panel so its weight can travel along a matching track.
functions: Support the moving sash or panel
Reduce sliding friction
Maintain panel height and alignment in the track

cad.pattern: Two or more rollers beneath each moving sash or panel
cad.placement: In the bottom rail running on the sill track
cad.opening: Moves continuously along the track
cad.load: Carries the moving panel weight

objects.name: sliding window or door track
objects.definition: A continuous rail or channel in the frame head, sill or threshold that guides a sliding sash or glazed-door panel and may carry its rollers.
functions: Define the panel travel line
Support rollers at the sill or threshold
Restrain the panel at the head and separate adjacent tracks

cad.pattern: Continuous horizontal run for each moving panel line
cad.placement: In the sill or threshold and matching head guide
cad.opening: Guides movement within the product plane
cad.load: Lower track carries panel weight; upper track usually restrains and guides

objects.name: window or glazed-door operating handle
objects.definition: A hand-operated fitting attached to a sash or door panel so a user can grip, lift, slide, pull, push or turn the moving part.
functions: Provide a user grip
Apply operating force to the sash or panel
Integrate with a latch or lock where designed

cad.pattern: One or more handles at reachable operating points
cad.placement: On the moving sash or door panel
cad.opening: Moves with the sash or panel
cad.load: Transfers user operating force to the moving part

objects.name: window or glazed-door lock and latch
objects.definition: A mechanical fitting that holds a window sash or glazed-door panel closed by engaging a keeper, jamb, meeting member or adjacent panel.
functions: Hold the moving part closed
Compress weatherseals where designed
Restrict unauthorised opening when lockable

cad.pattern: Discrete or multi-point mechanism along the closing edge
cad.placement: Between moving sash or panel and frame or meeting member
cad.opening: Engages only at the closed position
cad.load: Carries closing, seal-compression and security actions

objects.name: external glazed-door hinge
objects.definition: A pivoting fitting joining a hinged glazed-door leaf to its frame or joining adjacent folding leaves so they can swing relative to one another.
functions: Support or connect the door leaf
Define the swing axis
Transfer leaf weight and operating actions to the frame or adjacent panel

cad.pattern: Repeated hinges along a leaf edge or between folding panels
cad.placement: At the swinging vertical joint
cad.opening: Rotates through the leaf swing
cad.load: Carries door-leaf weight and hinge actions

objects.name: window flyscreen assembly
objects.definition: A removable or fixed insect screen made from mesh held in a light frame and fitted over the opening portion of a window.
functions: Exclude insects while allowing air flow
Fit within or against the window opening
Remain removable or serviceable where designed

cad.pattern: One framed mesh panel over each screened operable light
cad.placement: Inside or outside the moving sash according to product type
cad.opening: Covers the ventilation opening
cad.load: Insect screen only unless separately qualified for fall or security loads

notes: Ordinary flyscreen construction must not be assumed to satisfy fall-protection or security-screen requirements.

objects.name: flyscreen frame
objects.definition: The light perimeter frame that tensions and supports insect-screen mesh and fits the completed flyscreen into the window product.
functions: Hold the screen mesh flat
Provide edges for spline and clips
Fit the screen into a window channel or against the frame

cad.pattern: Closed rectangular frame around the screen mesh
cad.placement: At the perimeter of the flyscreen panel
cad.opening: Surrounds the mesh field
cad.load: Light screen support only unless separately tested

objects.name: flyscreen mesh
objects.definition: A fine open mesh stretched across a flyscreen frame to block insects while permitting ventilation and partial visibility.
functions: Exclude insects
Allow air to pass
Span between screen-frame edges under light tension

cad.pattern: Continuous mesh field clipped by the screen-frame perimeter
cad.placement: Across the flyscreen frame
cad.opening: Fills the screen frame with repeated apertures
cad.load: Light insect barrier unless separately qualified

objects.name: window opening restrictor
objects.definition: A fixed or releasable device attached between a window sash and frame to limit how far the openable part can move.
functions: Limit the clear window opening
Resist outward force through its attachment
Permit controlled release or override only where the selected device provides it

ncc_references.relationship: An opening-restricting device is one physical option for required bedroom-window protection, subject to the stated opening, force and release conditions.

cad.pattern: One or more limit devices at product-specific attachment points
cad.placement: Between openable sash and fixed frame
cad.opening: Becomes taut or stops travel at the permitted opening
cad.load: Fall-prevention restraint only when its complete installed system is qualified

notes: The ontology identifies the device; project logic must evaluate height, room use, fall distance, opening size, test evidence and release conditions.

objects.name: window fall-protection screen assembly
objects.definition: A securely fitted framed screen designed and installed to protect an openable window opening against a person falling through it.
functions: Cover the openable window area
Limit passage through the screen openings
Transfer outward actions through secure fittings to the window or building

ncc_references.relationship: A securely fitted screen is one physical option in the openable-window protection provisions, subject to stated project conditions.

cad.pattern: One robust framed screen across the protected openable area
cad.placement: Internal or external face of the window opening as documented
cad.opening: Covers the fall-risk opening while retaining small apertures
cad.load: Fall-protection assembly only when tested and installed as a complete system

notes: Security, insect and fall-protection performance are separate claims even where one proprietary screen supplies more than one role.

objects.name: child-resistant window-protection release mechanism
objects.definition: A physical release, lock or override mechanism on a removable or openable window restrictor or fall-protection screen, arranged to resist operation by a young child.
functions: Control removal or override of the protection device
Permit authorised release where the system allows it
Maintain the protected state against casual child operation

ncc_references.relationship: A removable, unlockable or overridable screen or device in the stated bedroom-window case requires a child-resistant release mechanism.

cad.pattern: One release mechanism at the documented accessible control point
cad.placement: On the restrictor or protected screen fitting
cad.opening: Controls whether the protection assembly can open or be removed
cad.load: Control fitting, not the primary load-resisting screen attachment

objects.name: window or glazed-door weatherseal assembly
objects.definition: The coordinated seals around moving sashes or door panels and their meeting joints, selected so the closed product restricts air and water movement while still operating.
functions: Restrict air leakage through operable joints
Reduce water entry at closed edges
Accommodate repeated opening, compression or sliding movement

ncc_references.relationship: Openable window and door edges may require seals to restrict air infiltration according to the stated climate and space conditions.

cad.pattern: Continuous or interrupted seal runs around moving perimeters and meeting joints
cad.placement: In grooves or on contact faces between sash or panel and frame
cad.opening: Compresses, wipes or separates as the product opens
cad.load: Flexible environmental seal, not a structural connection

notes: Glazing seals between glass and frame are catalogued separately from weatherseals around moving parts.

objects.name: compression weatherseal
objects.definition: A resilient strip or hollow profile that is compressed between a closed sash or door panel and its frame to restrict air and water passage.
functions: Close the moving perimeter under compression
Recover shape after opening
Accommodate small frame and hardware tolerances

cad.pattern: Continuous strip around compression-closing edges
cad.placement: Between closed sash or leaf and frame stop or rebate
cad.opening: Separates from the contact face when opened
cad.load: Flexible seal under controlled compression

objects.name: woven pile sliding weatherseal
objects.definition: A woven brush-like pile strip fitted in a carrier groove to wipe and seal sliding sashes or door panels while tolerating movement and small clearances.
functions: Reduce air passage at sliding joints
Wipe against the adjoining profile during motion
Compensate for small tolerance variations

cad.pattern: Continuous seal runs along sliding contact and interlock lines
cad.placement: In grooves of sash, panel, jamb, track or interlock profiles
cad.opening: Maintains wiping contact during sliding
cad.load: Low-friction environmental seal

notes: Woolpile is an industry name; most modern pile seals are synthetic rather than wool.

objects.name: external door bottom draft-protection seal
objects.definition: A sweep, compressible seal, automatic drop seal or similar device fitted along the bottom edge of an external door leaf to restrict air flow at the threshold.
functions: Restrict air infiltration below the closed door
Contact or drop onto the threshold
Allow the door to open without permanent obstruction

ncc_references.relationship: Where the building-sealing provision applies, the bottom edge of a door uses a draft-protection device.

cad.pattern: Continuous seal across the bottom edge of the moving leaf
cad.placement: At leaf underside or lower face above the threshold
cad.opening: Slides, lifts or retracts as the door opens
cad.load: Flexible or mechanical air seal

objects.name: window or door perimeter sealant joint assembly
objects.definition: The sealed installation joint between a window or door product and the surrounding wall, normally combining a controlled gap, backer rod or bond breaker, compatible sealant and prepared contact surfaces.
functions: Restrict air and water passage at the product perimeter
Accommodate limited movement between product and wall
Connect the product frame to adjacent weather and air-control layers

ncc_references.relationship: External-fabric frame openings and their junctions may require close-fitting trims, foam, compressible strips, caulking or similar seals according to the stated conditions.

cad.pattern: Continuous seal line around selected interior or exterior frame edges
cad.placement: In the gap between product frame or reveal and surrounding wall finish or substrate
cad.opening: Seals the perimeter without blocking required drainage paths
cad.load: Movement-capable environmental joint, not a structural frame fixing

notes: Sealant does not replace head, jamb and sill flashings where the opening detail requires them.

objects.name: window or door perimeter backer rod
objects.definition: A compressible foam rod inserted behind perimeter sealant to control joint depth, support tooling and prevent the sealant bonding to the back of the joint.
functions: Set the sealant depth
Provide a curved backing surface
Act as a bond breaker at the rear of the joint

cad.pattern: Continuous compressed rod behind the sealant bead
cad.placement: In the product-to-wall perimeter gap
cad.opening: Occupies the rear portion of the sealant joint
cad.load: Sealant support and bond breaker only

objects.name: window or door perimeter sealant bead
objects.definition: A tooled elastomeric bead bonded to the window or door frame and adjacent wall surface to close the exposed perimeter joint while allowing specified movement.
functions: Seal the exposed perimeter joint
Bridge limited movement between dissimilar components
Connect to adjacent air or water-control surfaces

cad.pattern: Continuous tooled bead over backer rod or bond breaker
cad.placement: At the visible interior or exterior product-to-wall joint
cad.opening: Closes the front portion of the joint
cad.load: Flexible environmental seal

notes: Compatibility with frame finish, membrane, flashing and cladding substrates must be verified for the selected system.
